learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover the universal laws of energy! Learn how heat flows, why certain chemical reactions happen spontaneously, and calculate the energy changes taking place in the world around you.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The 'System' is the specific part of the universe you are studying (like a beaker of chemicals). Everything else is the 'Surroundings'. Systems can be Open (exchange both energy and matter), Closed (exchange only energy), or Isolated (exchange nothing, like a perfect thermos).

Energy can neither be created nor destroyed. The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) of a system is equal to the heat ($q$) added to the system plus the work ($w$) done on the system. Mathematical formula: $\Delta U = q + w$.

Enthalpy is essentially the total heat content at constant pressure. Exothermic reactions release heat (Negative $\Delta H$), while Endothermic reactions absorb heat (Positive $\Delta H$). Hess's Law states that total enthalpy change is the same whether a reaction takes one step or multiple steps!

Entropy is the measure of randomness or disorder in a system. A solid melting to liquid increases entropy! The Second Law states that the entropy of the entire universe is constantly increasing. Nature loves chaos!

Will a reaction happen on its own? Gibbs Free Energy tells us! It combines Enthalpy and Entropy: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$. If $\Delta G$ is negative, the reaction is spontaneous. If positive, it won't happen without outside help.

fun_activity.title: 🥶 The Cold Pack Reaction
fun_activity.instructions: If you crack open a chemical sports cold pack, it instantly gets freezing cold. This is an 'Endothermic' reaction! It is pulling heat OUT of your hand and into the chemical system (Positive $\Delta H$), driven entirely by a massive increase in Entropy as the solid dissolves into liquid!

exam_tips: 📌 Be incredibly careful with Sign Conventions: Work done BY the system (expansion) is $-w$, and work done ON the system (compression) is $+w$. Heat absorbed is $+q$, heat released is $-q$.
📌 Distinguish between Intensive properties (independent of mass, like Temperature or Density) and Extensive properties (depend on mass, like Volume or Internal Energy).
📌 To check spontaneity, use the Gibbs equation. Even an endothermic reaction ($+\Delta H$) can be spontaneous if the temperature is high enough and the entropy change ($+\Delta S$) is large enough!
quick_recap: ⭐ State functions depend only on the initial and final states of the system, not on the path taken (e.g., Temperature, Pressure, Enthalpy). Work and Heat are NOT state functions; they are path functions.
⭐ The standard enthalpy of formation for any element in its most stable reference state (like $O_2$ gas or solid Carbon graphite) is exactly zero.
⭐ At equilibrium, the change in Gibbs Free energy ($\Delta G$) is exactly zero.
